items.title: Public Preview: JWT validation with Azure Front Door Auth Policy
items.description:
JSON Web Token (JWT) validation through Azure Front Door Auth Policy is now in public preview on Azure Front Door Premium. Validate bearer tokens issued by Microsoft Entra ID at the edge before requests reach your APIs or web applications, helping you centralize authentication checks and reduce unnecessary traffic to your origins.

Associate an Auth Policy with a profile, domain, or route, and configure the expected issuer and audience for token validation. Use Block mode to reject requests with missing or invalid tokens with an HTTP 401 Unauthorized response or evaluate requests without blocking them in Log mode. This preview focuses on validating existing bearer tokens; your application remains responsible for application-specific authorization, and origin access should be restricted to prevent clients from bypassing Azure Front Door.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Front Door mutual TLS authentication
items.description:
Mutual TLS (mTLS), also known as client certificate authentication, is now generally available on Azure Front Door Premium. Use X.509 client certificates to help protect sensitive applications and APIs in business-to-business, Internet of Things, financial services, and enterprise scenarios. 

Choose from four modes: require and validate, require without validation, validate when presented, or pass through to the origin. These modes let you control whether client certificates are mandatory and whether Azure Front Door or your origin performs certificate validation. When forwarded to the origin, the client certificate is provided in the X-Azure-ClientCertificate request header. 

General availability also simplifies trusted CA configuration. You can upload only the trusted root CA certificate to Azure Key Vault and associate it with your Front Door custom domain, without uploading intermediate CA certificates. With this configuration, clients must present their client certificate and all required intermediate certificates during the TLS handshake. When edge validation is enabled, Azure Front Door builds and validates the certificate chain at request time against the configured trusted root CA.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Auto scaling of ingestion limits in Azure Monitor workspace
items.description:
Auto scaling introduces a per-workspace capability in Azure Monitor Workspace (AMW) to automatically scale ingestion limits based on observed usage patterns. When enabled, the system dynamically adjusts ingestion limits (quota ceiling) to maintain healthy utilization and reduce the need for manual limit management. Limits are increased as your metrics volume grows and can be decreased when usage stays low for a sustained period of time.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: SQL performance monitoring for Azure SQL Managed Instance
items.description:
The public preview of Microsoft-managed performance monitoring for Azure SQL Managed Instance is now available. 

Customers monitoring business-critical SQL Managed Instance workloads often rely on custom scripts and disconnected monitoring tools. This requires them to manage telemetry infrastructure and manually correlate performance insights across their SQL Managed Instance estate. 

The new experience collects and stores performance telemetry and provides resource-level and at-scale dashboards to help identify performance trends, anomalies, and resource bottlenecks. For deeper analysis and custom visualizations, you can securely query their monitoring data using Kusto Query Language (KQL) through an RBAC-protected Azure Data Explorer proxy endpoint. 

Learn more:
